messages.author: 6034c700b2af7b7b
messages.subject: subsetting a data set: simple question
parts:
Hello!

I have all my data in one large spreadsheet, but need to be able to subset it without leaving "blank" spaces.  Its a fairly large matrix of bee x plant interactions, that needs to be subset by year, site, date, and flower.  The end goal is to run it through metaMDS.

when I use the bracket sub-setting approach []:
bee2013<-all.bee[all.bee$y2013==1,]
Where 
all.bee = complete data set
y2013 =  a variable where if the data was collected in 2013, =1, if any other year =0.
I then use bee2013 to crate a table of bee/plant x site.

It will not allow me to use a table drawn from bee2011 to run through metaMDS and gives me this error output:

Wisconsin double standardization
Error in if (any(dist < -sqrt(.Machine$double.eps))) warning("some dissimilarities are negative -- is this intentional?") : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In distfun(comm, method = distance, ...) :
  you have empty rows: their dissimilarities may be meaningless in method bray

2: In distfun(comm, method = distance, ...) : missing values in results

(additional comment:  it works for the whole dataset, so there aren't any hidden problems in my original .csv)

Any better suggestions?  It should just be a simple split the data by year, but without leaving ghost spaces that metaMDS still tries to use to ordinate my community data.

Thanks!
Jenny

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: subsetting a data set: simple question
parts:
Attached is a file called example data, I just used excel to filer out 75% of the data, to just look at one flower species Penstemon rydbergii.

I'd like a table of insect species ("g_sp") by site ( "site") to ordinate in metaMDS.  Ideally I'd love to not have to use the "yearsitetype" column, so that I can get r to connect the dots as each site is replicated across years in ordination space.  (what I mean is, I am using a long term data set to see how communities at each site change, so I would ordinate all communities in all years, then connect site A in 2011 to A in 2012 to A in 2013... etc).  For this example, use the "site" since I am asking to subset the whole dataset to just one year, 2012.
 

all.bee<-choose.csv()
bee2012<-all.bee[all.bee$y2012==1,]
sitebee12<-table(bee2012$site, bee2012$g_sp)
bee12sitetype<-metaMDS(sitebee12,k=2)
plot(bee12sitetype, type = "n")
text(bee12sitetype, display = "sites", cex = 0.7, col="black")
text(bee12sitetype, display = "species", cex = 0.5, col="slate blue")

messages.author: 4742ff1f9fc5f9ca
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: subsetting a data set: simple question
parts:
Jenny,

I've had this problem before. Having zeros throughout a row (i.e. some site type had no bees) or a column (some bee species was never encountered) makes it hard to calculate a dissimilarity matrix. Likewise, rows with identical occurrences are problematic because their dissimilarity will be zero. The best options will be to use all years of data together if that helps eliminate the zero problem. Otherwise, you may have to start removing site types and species to the point where you can calculate a dissimilarity matrix.

-Matt

parts:
Hi Jenny,

I haven't read the thread in detail, but could this be related to not dropping factor levels?  Is 'bee' a factor?
It may be that not dropping the empty bee levels is causing the zero rows.  ...just a hunch.

-Dan.

Matt Whalen
March 26, 2014 at 3:48 PM

Jenny,

I've had this problem before. Having zeros throughout a row (i.e. some site type had no bees) or a column (some bee species was never encountered) makes it hard to calculate a dissimilarity matrix. Likewise, rows with identical occurrences are problematic because their dissimilarity will be zero. The best options will be to use all years of data together if that helps eliminate the zero problem. Otherwise, you may have to start removing site types and species to the point where you can calculate a dissimilarity matrix.

-Matt

Dan’s hunch looks right! I was working on a solution and adding droplevels did the trick. Here’s a quick workflow to run the ordination for all years:

require(plyr)
require(vegan)
all.bee = read.csv("jvw_exampledata_penryd1.csv")
# The following creates a list of metaMDS models for each year
# You could use .(site, year) to split up by each site and then
# table(d$species, d$g_sp) to look at plant-pollinator relationships
#in each site/year combination
l = dlply(all.bee, .(year), function(d) {
      d = droplevels(d)
      t = table(d$site, d$g_sp)
      metaMDS(t,k=2)
   })
#Plot the first model
plot(l[[1]], type = "n")
text(l[[1]], display = "sites", cex = 0.7, col="black")

Noam
